variants.name: A · 展开绘本
variants.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Create ONE polished full-screen landscape 16:9 Chinese game battle UI concept, not a collage, no outer device frame, no version title or annotation. Target a playable Godot match-3 + card roguelite. Reference image 1 provides established character identities and gameplay UI; image 2 provides approved paper-theatre art language. Redesign substantially, do not copy reference layout pixel-for-pixel.
All four concepts use identical gameplay state, play-card phase, so make this screen understandable on its own. One central square match-three board, EXACTLY 8 columns by 8 rows = 64 equal square cells. Carefully count eight pieces per row, eight rows. Six tile types ONLY: cyan ice snowflake, red flame, violet lightning bolt, mint wind spiral, gold four-point star resource, blue shield resource. Do not use the sun or dark vortex as board tiles. Clean distinguishable glossy paper tokens, no large visual effects obscuring cells. Central board the largest visual target. Place hand below board, never shrink board to fit hand.
White-haired chibi female sticker hero 柯莱塔 left, purple chibi monster 连击体 right, close to reference. Player readable compact info: "柯莱塔 · Lv.2", "生命 51/65", "格挡 5", "攻击 7", "经验 1/4". Three red journey hearts and silver shell currency "35", separate from combat HP. Six skill-point icons with counts: snowflake4 flame2 lightning3 wind1 sun0 vortex0. Player side three supply slots, two small bottle icons and one empty. Enemy "连击体", "生命 32/40", "格挡 0". Highly legible enemy intent panel "下一次行动" and "攻击 3 × 2". Phase heading "第 3 回合", "消除 → 出牌", active 出牌. Clear bottom-right ticket button "结束回合". Utility controls "地图", "记录", "撤退", small "藏品" and "规则". Draw/discard piles "抽牌堆 8" and "弃牌堆 2".
Exactly five illustrated cards across bottom center with readable names/effects: cost 1 ice "碎晶弹" / "造成 7 点伤害"; cost 1 ice "护身晶幕" / "获得 5 格挡"; cost 1 ice "交错射击" / "伤害 3 · 格挡 3"; cost 1 flame "点火" / "本回合攻击力 +2"; cost 2 ice "晶簇狙击" / "造成 17 点伤害". Crisp beautiful illustrated card art with distinct silhouettes, cream description areas, no lorem ipsum. Middle card subtly raised with gold hover rim, bottom card texts remain visible. Chinese type clean and readable, exact short text, avoid microtext and clutter. Treat figures as concept sample values not invented new mechanics.
Keep decorative scenery low contrast and on margins, no map paths, no unnecessary banners, no subtitle explaining interface, no English, no watermark. Gold/cream/plum palette with coral red primary action; richly illustrated, refined, usable UI, not a flat wireframe.

DIRECTION A — OPEN STORYBOOK BATTLE. Closest continuation of approved map. Wide open ivory parchment book across whole frame, center spine behind board, restrained burgundy curtains top corners, paper castle silhouettes embossed on page edges. Center board dark desaturated plum inset board with thin gold stitched border occupying about 42% width and 67% height, positioned upper-middle. Left player's ivory book page in neatly spaced blocks occupying 24%, right enemy's page same width. Both characters medium sized, not oversized. Cream landscape paper intent ticket below enemy. Hand cards arranged in a gentle shallow fan on book bottom edge, five cards equal height with middle hover. Status top left on a translucent dark plum strip, phase paper bookmark above board, tickets feel handcrafted with stitched edges, lavish but highly organized. Warm daylight on textured paper, soft dimensional cut-paper shadows. Strong book silhouette, gold corner clasps. This should be a new battle screen in exactly the same art family as reference map.

DIRECTION B — PAPER PUPPET THEATRE. A frontal jewel-box miniature stage with open deep aubergine curtains, warm ivory and dusty lavender layered castle silhouettes. No giant book. Two paper chibi characters stand on small layered plinths left and right with white die-cut outlines, environment visible behind them, minimal enclosing panels. Center match board suspended like an ornate square theatre prop with scalloped cream outer frame and muted lilac cells, clear 8x8 grid. Top round central star medallion integrates phase ticket. Lower stage front is an elegant horizontal hand-card tray, cards slightly tilted in shallow fan, draw/discard small tickets at tray left, coral-red action ticket at tray right. More spatial depth and character presence than reference, balanced bright playable central area, restrained golden hanging stars only near top. No scenic decorations crossing board or card text. Soft miniature stage lighting, premium paper craft illustration.

DIRECTION C — MIDNIGHT STAR BOARD. A sophisticated midnight plum and ink-violet tabletop UI, no curtains and no open book. Center 8x8 board mounted in a dark velvet-lined square wooden game box, very thin antique gold edge, dark satin cells providing excellent bright token readability. Fine constellation pinpricks and engraved stars confined to outer corners; predominantly quiet background. Side information appears in slim dark plum cards with cream type and hairline gold borders; chibi characters remain colorful paper stickers in small circular medallions upper sides. Cream intent ticket on right is the strongest contrast besides central board. Six resource pips in orderly 2x3 block left. Bottom five cards stand nearly straight in an evenly spaced rack, cream names/effects and dark illustrated centers, middle selected rim glowing warm gold. Header slim and dark with phase a small cream capsule; very readable large coral action ticket bottom right. Rich tactical boardgame atmosphere, matte premium materials and tiny gold accents, not neon sci-fi. Stronger hierarchy and focus than theatrical reference.

Central square 8x8 grid with pale lavender-gray wells and thin ivory dividers, tokens deep saturated jewel colors so they remain readable. Generous clean margins and orderly rectangular cut-paper modules, soft tactile shadows and a few small corner star stamps only.
